ECE 6390

DVB-S2: from payload to waveform

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows how a useful bit stream passes through the protection and waveform stages of a satellite broadcast.

DVB-S2 supplies selectable satellite modulation-and-coding profiles. In the transmit chain, an outer BCH block code adds protection, an inner LDPC code adds further constraints, a mapper assigns coded bits to symbols, and physical framing supplies synchronization and optional pilots. A receiver reverses these roles after synchronizing. Bit interleaving is used for 8PSK and APSK; the QPSK path bypasses that interleaver.

For occupied raised-cosine RF width B and rolloff α, the channel sends Rs = B/(1+α) symbols per second. Each mapped data symbol carries m = log₂M coded bits. The rate during mapped symbols is mRs. Across a complete physical frame, only a fraction ηPL of the symbols carry these bits, giving a frame-average coded bit rate of ηPL mRs. Coding and the baseband header further reduce the useful payload rate.

A normal FEC frame contains 64,800 LDPC-coded bits, or 64,800/m mapped symbols. Each physical frame adds a 90-symbol header. When enabled, 36-symbol pilot blocks follow every 16 slots of 90 mapped symbols, except at the frame boundary. If the transmitted frame lasts T seconds, the frame-average coded bit rate is 64,800/T. The filled-frame payload rate is (KBCH − 80)/T, where KBCH is the BCH input length and 80 bits carry the baseband header.

Each profile pairs a supported inner code rate with a constellation. The figure assumes a full baseband frame and excludes input-packet and padding losses. The lecture’s inner-LDPC rates span 1/4 through 9/10. At the QPSK end, lowering rate can provide more protection while reducing useful throughput. These controls account for resource usage. Link feasibility also needs a profile’s required received quality and a selected error target.

Example

For a 6 MHz channel, QPSK at α = 0.35 carries 8.89 Mbit/s during mapped symbols. At α = 0.20, 32APSK carries 25 Mbit/s during mapped symbols, a ratio of 2.8125. With the figure’s QPSK 3/4 profile, α = 0.25 and pilots on, the same channel sends 4.8 Msym/s. Its 33,282-symbol frame lasts 6.934 ms. The 64,800 coded bits average 9.346 Mbit/s, and the 48,328 payload bits average 6.970 Mbit/s.

Practice

1. Why does selecting a listed inner rate 3/4 fail to establish that 75% of every RF symbol is useful payload?

Follow both coding stages and the framing resources.

BCH parity, the baseband header, the physical header and any pilots also use resources. The useful fraction needs the complete chain, not only the inner-LDPC ratio.

2. If a fade already forced QPSK, how can the system trade still more throughput for protection?

A MODCOD contains a coding choice as well as a constellation.

It can choose a supported lower coding rate. More of the transmitted stream then carries redundancy, reducing useful information rate while potentially improving reliability for the stated decoder.
